For a while now I had been wanting to get the It Cosmetics Heavenly Luxe Airbrush Powder & Bronzer Brush #1, but then I was also considering the It Cosmetics Brushes for Ulta Fluffy All Over Powder Brush #211. I ended up getting the It Cosmetics #1 brush and absolutely love it. Then, I saw this! This is a large powder brush. It’s about 7.5 inches long. The hairs are about 1.5 inches long and go across about 2.5 inches! It’s definitely a big fluffy brush! It is densely packed, but still fluffy! They say it has “over 100,000 ultra-plush, fluffy synthetic hairs.” I definitely believe it! The hairs are SOOOO soft! I’ve always thought that my It Cosmetics brushes were the softest, fluffiest I’ve ever felt. But this is on par with those! It’s seriously amazing how great this brush is for such an unbelievable price! (I took photos comparing it to my It #7 brush). This is definitely longer than the It #7, which is a kabuki style, and the head is slightly bigger. But it’s just as soft and just as fluffy, and I reach for this more for powder than the #7. After trying this out for a little bit, I immediately went to see if they had any other brushes in a similar style. I saw they had a dual ended foundation/concealer brush that looks exactly like the It Cosmetics Heavenly Luxe Complexion Perfection Brush #7, which I also have and use regularly….so I grabbed that to compare it too! At $9.99 I couldn’t pass it up. I paid $49 for my It brush and I’d been wanting a backup but wasn’t willing to fork over another $49 to have a duplicate that I didn’t really NEED. But, for $9.99 I definitely was!

This brush is absolutely amazing! It’s so soft and fluffy, but still dense enough to apply powder well. It is soft, but doesn’t have that silky, slippery overly synthetic feel some synthetic brushes have. I hate when synthetic brushes have that silky/slippery feel where product just kind of fall off the hairs. So, I was really happy these hairs weren’t like that! They pick up powder well and apply it beautifully! This has become my go to powder brush and I can’t recommend it enough!

The one thing that I did find wasn’t accurate on the product page was that the knots are bleached. I’ve seen some product pages say “slightly bleached knots,” which I’ve always taken to mean that some knots are bleached and some aren’t. Why they do some and not all, I don’t know. Probably so that it doesn’t cause as much shedding as bleaching all the knots would. But, that’s just as guess. Anyways, I’d definitely say this wig has slightly bleached knots. Some are bleached, you can’t see the knots at all. Others are NOT bleached. I added a photo to show. The ones in the front center aren’t bleached at all. You can clearly see a ton of dark knots. On the sides there are a few dark knots, but they don’t seem as dark as the ones in the front center and there’s a lot that you can’t see that are bleached.

Now, some people like knots bleached and some don’t like bleached knots. If you don’t know about knots, lace wigs have the hair tied onto the lace, creating knots. Now, if the hair is lighter in color at the lace, this isn’t a big deal since basically the knots are already bleached. But, when the hair is darker in color at the lace, like this one, the knots are a lot more noticeable. So, some wigs come with those knots bleached so they aren’t as noticeable. And, if they don’t come bleached, then some people bleach the knots themselves. Bleaching knots makes it so the knots are less noticeable, making the lace wig look even more natural. But, bleaching knots has its downsides. To bleach the knots, you’re doing a chemical process on the hairs to lighten the knots. This will chemically alter the hair. It opens the cuticles and removes the color. By making the knots lighter it hides the tiny knots and creates the illusion that the hair is growing from your scalp. But, this has its cons. Bleaching the knots makes them weaker, which leads to the hair shedding faster. The darker the hair is means the more colors it needs to go through to get bleached, which makes the knot even weaker. It also takes some skill to bleach the knots and not effect the rest of the hair. So, most people who like bleached knots prefer to get a wig that already has bleached knots.

This wig comes in 6 different lengths - 18”, 20”, 22”, 24”, 26”, and 28”. A huge pet peeve of mine with product pages for wigs I see sold here on Amazon is companies using the same exact photos for all the different options. There’s a HUGE difference between the length of 18 inches and the length of 28 inches. But, all the product photos are the exact same for all the length options (aside from the first photo for a couple has different photos of real women. BUT the rest of the photos, specifically the photos of the wig on the mannequin are the EXACT SAME for all the lengths. There isn’t anything showing people what the length will look like for each separate option. Just the same photo of the same length wig for every single length option! Some people may be purchasing a wig for the first time, or be trying out a new length and not know how different 18 inches looks compared to 28 inches. It’s ridiculous to me to ask people to spend their hard earned money, especially at this price point, and not be able to provide them with at least a couple photos showing the actual length of each option. It’s not that hard to have a photo of the wig on a mannequin head showing the actual length for each option instead of the same one for all options! Looking at the hair they are showing on the mannequin, my guess is it’s around 20” or 22”. So, it would be easy for someone to look at the photos when looking at the 18 inch option, and think that’s what the length will look like. Only for it to arrive and be shorter, creating a disappointed customer. It makes no sense to me why companies do this, but I see it constantly on here and it’s become a huge annoyance to me! Anyways, enough about that…

Overall, I think the wig is beautiful. The hair is full and healthy looking. It’s soft. It didn’t shed much. It’s plucked nicely and the baby hairs look good. If you don’t mind that all the knots aren’t bleached and you know what length to expect and don’t go by the product photos, I think you’d be happy with this wig.
